name: Transition
identity_check: Confirmed as Transition (transition.vc; operated by Transition Global Management Limited, FCA FRN 994544, per the site footer), a London-based (5 Carnaby Street) cross-Atlantic climate and deep tech fund that David Helgason (Unity co-founder) launched in 2021 and that backs pre-seed to Series A founders in Europe, the UK and the US. 'Transition Ventures' is the same firm: transition.vc links the LinkedIn page 'Transition Ventures' (which links back to transition.vc) and the Substack transitionvc.substack.com, published as 'Transition Ventures'; TechCrunch, TNW, ImpactAlpha and Construct Capital also use that name. It is NOT the Bengaluru 'Transition VC' (India's energy-transition fund co-founded by Shoeb Ali and Raiyaan Shingati, Rs 700 Cr debut fund closed Dec 2025, backer of Matel, CIMware, Hydgen), which shares the name but has no link to transition.vc. Nor is it Transition Metal Solutions, a portfolio company.

conflicts.reason: Both reports give $150M; ImpactAlpha leads with a euro figure, so the fund may be euro-denominated. The firm's own site states no fund size, and neither article says whether this is a final close.

open_items: Fund I: size and close date not published. ImpactAlpha says the debut fund closed under two years before June 2026 'at a similar size' (about $150M), and TNW gives AUM over $300M; TechCrunch (2024) says Transition does not disclose fund sizes. A search-result hint (CB Insights, not opened) shows a 'Transition Global I Fund' of $77.8M closed Dec 2025, which matches the Indian Transition VC's Rs 700 Cr fund and is probably a conflation. No Companies House or FCA register filing was checked.

Wrong-firm risk: data/research/cache/catamaran-ventures.json records Matel's Rs 130 Cr Series B (Aug 2026) with participant 'Transition VC', and Matel's May 2024 Series A was led by 'Transition VC'. Both refer to the Bengaluru firm (Shoeb Ali, Raiyaan Shingati), not this London firm (Entrackr and SolarQuarter pages listed here). inv_transition-vc in data/processed already shows a mobility_ev portfolio weight that likely comes from that round; it needs a merge block (this file does not touch other files).

Rounds not recorded for lack of a fetchable page naming Transition: Skye (Stockholm industrial energy autopilot; search snippets say an ~$11M seed in Dec 2025 led by London-based Transition with Course Corrected, Sondo, Byfounders, Emblem, Hawktail; Nordic9 and Techleap returned 403); Valor (electrochemical metals refining; a Valor social post, not opened, reportedly says a $5M+ first round co-led by Transition Ventures; the Transition post gives no terms); Kerrigan (AI factory operating system, pre-seed, San Francisco per Transition's companies page; no announcement found, Wellfound 403); Upway (Transition invested in 2022 per TNW, but the 2022 Series A articles opened name only Sequoia and Exor); OLIX's first institutional round in 2024 (Transition 'came in at the first round'; terms never announced) and its Feb 2026 $220M round led by Hummingbird (Transition's participation not stated).

Seven further portfolio companies are listed as 'to be announced' on the companies page (e.g. space-based energy structures, unmanned-fleet coordination, materials discovery for microelectronics), so they cannot be recorded yet.
Volter seed (Nov 2024): amount and co-investors not found; only Transition's own post was available.

Application URL: none. The site has no pitch form, only a general hello@ address (not recorded) and 'We like to get to know you as early as possible.' Cold inbound left unknown because no page explicitly invites unsolicited pitches.

requires_us_entity = no is inferred from the stated Europe/UK/US remit and from portfolio companies based in London, Eindhoven and Copenhagen; no page states a policy. Nothing found on Indian founders.

portfolio_count_reported = 15 is as of Nov 2024 (Volter was 'Transition's 15th investment'). Earlier counts: 9 companies (Northstack, Aug 2023), 12 (TechCrunch, Jun 2024). The Oct 2026 companies page lists 10 announced and 7 unannounced current companies, plus Watershed and Secondlaw as featured, with a 'See more' link.

Partner focus sectors are inferred from bios and from the deals each person wrote up or was quoted on; no page gives formal focus areas. No individual LinkedIn URLs appear on the team page. Mona Alsubaei (partner per Northstack 2023, author of 2025 posts) is not on the current team page and is not recorded.
